chunks: And ʿĀmir ibn Nuʿaym al-Qummī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About the dwellings in which people stay, wherein there is the urine of animals and dung, and which are entered by the Jews and the Christians—what should we do regarding salat (prayer) in them?
So he said: “Pray on your garment.”

key_terms.الْمَنَازِلِ: dwellings or places where people stay

ai.seo_question: How should one perform salat (prayer) in a place suspected of impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) in places that may be affected by impurity, such as animal urine and dung. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs the questioner to pray on his garment, indicating a practical way to avoid direct contact with potentially impure ground.
